notes: Reference food: Glucose/2.5 h. Used for bengali_khichuri. Only candidate: T1-664; T1-663 is barnyard millet khichdi, a different grain. Khichuri is the Bengali name for khichdi: rice and dal cooked soft together. The compendium does not name the dal, and our recipe adds potato, cauliflower and peas.

Reference food: Glucose/2 h. Used for steamed_rice. Only candidate: T1-666, white rice cooked with water at 1:2 (the serving column). Not used: T1-619 to T1-621 are parboiled varieties, T1-683 to T1-685 are one parboiled variety at three degrees of polish (ref 141), T1-633 is basmati and T1-665 a high-fibre variety.

Reference food: Glucose/2 h. Used for chapati. Candidates, each a plain wheat chapati or roti from an Indian study: T1-711 (44.6), T1-673 (48.37), T1-691 (54.43), T1-657 (64), T1-631 (83.92); this is the median. Not used: T1-615 to T1-618, T1-632, T1-651, T1-674 and T1-712 add amaranth, rice bran, sorghum, carrot or multigrain flour.

Reference food: Glucose/2 h. Used for rava_upma. Candidates, each a semolina upma from an Indian study: T1-658 (58), T1-697 (62.37), T1-659 (67); this is the median. Not used: T1-628 and T1-630 are vermicelli (sewai) upma, T1-652 and T1-653 sorghum, T1-707 to T1-709 add finger millet, T1-048 was tested in Singapore.

Reference food: Glucose/2 h. Used for idli. Candidates, each a plain idli from an Indian study: T1-698 (62.45) and T1-627 (67.11); with two, the lower middle value is used. Not used: T1-629 (kodo millet idli), T1-046 (tested in Singapore), T1-842 to T1-847 (idli eaten with sambol or sampar).

Reference food: Glucose/2 h. Used for methi_thepla. Only candidate: T1-699; T1-700 adds ashwagandha. The compendium does not say whether this thepla had methi leaves; thepla is a wheat flatbread cooked on a tawa with oil, like our recipe.
